title: project.activate mints its own measured witness and refuses a caller-supplied one
description:
SPIDR child B of task-bb844c288fb346c0856778c738b9f073. dependsOn child A (task-741dad13e23d441a8385d0f14df5b5c1) for the receipts module. Filed by architect-d1711c47 2026-09-04, measured at main 68eb1c5d.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the daemon stops trusting the caller for the activation witness and mints it from child A's measured receipts. This is the row that closes the actual product gap - today ANY caller can hand over invented refs and the daemon commits them.

MEASURED AT 68eb1c5d:
- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts:108-120 `activateProject` reads `payload.witness`, refuses BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID @ DAEMON_INGRESS when absent, and otherwise passes the CALLER'S OBJECT STRAIGHT INTO the core reducer. Nothing measures anything.
- TWO fakers exist today, not one. (1) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/demo-seed-payloads.ts:127-137 (the seed). (2) apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts:111-119 `DEV_PAYLOADS`, whose witness is artifact-1/backup-1/hex64("cafe") and which tests/e2e/control-room/board-chain.spec.ts clicks end-to-end from an EMPTY store. So "the browser cannot drive the chain" is only true of the v2 UI; the legacy dev board drives it with fake refs.
- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:314 declares `"project.activate": ["witness"]` as the payload key roster - changing what the payload may carry is a roster edit here, and the roster has asserting tests.
- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:31 and :107 hold project.activate's prerequisite chain (register + bind_repository + provider.probe).
- packages/core/src/project/project-validation.ts:158 validActivation demands the EXACT 9 keys, real 64-hex for the two hashes, and truthClass in {DAEMON_VERIFIED, HUMAN_APPROVED}.

DESIGN (settled at plan time, do not re-derive): the browser sends `project.activate` and the DAEMON measures. A witness that crosses the wire could be altered by a hostile caller, so a caller-supplied `witness` is REFUSED with its own stable code rather than ignored - silently dropping it would let an operator believe they supplied authority they did not. When every member measures, the handler mints the 9-key witness with truthClass DAEMON_VERIFIED and commits. When ANY member is unmeasurable, the WHOLE activation refuses with that member's code from child A - fail closed, no partial witness, nothing committed.

KEEP WORKING (parent DoD 4): `pnpm seed` must still pass. The seed sends its own witness, so this change WILL break it unless the seed is updated in the same commit - update demo-seed-payloads.ts/demo-seed-plan.ts to stop sending one, and keep the chain ORDER in demo-seed-plan.ts:190-196 unchanged. The same applies to DEV_PAYLOADS in live-dispatch-payloads.ts and to board-chain.spec.ts's expectations.

NOT IN SCOPE: the receipts read route and the UI card (child C); the e2e journey, copy and docs (child D).

implementationPlan.description: CARRY THE RECEIPTS THE WAY `humanReview` TRAVELS. In `bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts`, add an OPTIONAL `receipts?: ActivationReceiptSet` to `HandlerContext` (type imported from child A's `bootstrap/activation-receipts.js`). In `bootstrap-services.ts`, give `runBootstrapCommand` a receipts parameter alongside `humanReview` and thread it into the context object the same way — spread rather than assigned, because under exactOptionalPropertyTypes an explicit `undefined` is a DIFFERENT thing from an absent key. THE POINT OF THIS SHAPE: receipts reach the handler only from the CALLER'S arguments, so a request payload structurally cannot present them — the identical guarantee the humanReview comment already documents. Do NOT make `CommandHandler` async: that would change every handler's type and every call site, and the async-entry mechanism in the next step exists precisely so you do not have to.

MINT, AND REFUSE THE CALLER'S. Rewrite `activateProject` in `bootstrap-services.ts:108-120`. New order: (1) if `request.payload` carries a `witness` key at all, refuse ACTIVATION_WITNESS_CALLER_SUPPLIED at DAEMON_INGRESS and commit nothing — refuse rather than silently ignore, or an operator would believe they supplied authority they did not; (2) if `context.receipts` is absent, refuse (the sync path cannot measure, and a defaulted witness is exactly the defect this row closes); (3) if ANY receipt member is `known:false`, refuse the WHOLE activation with THAT MEMBER'S code and layer from child A — no partial witness, no defaulted member, nothing committed; (4) otherwise build the EXACT 9-key witness from the measured values — `artifactPathRef`, `backupPathRef`, `credentialRef`, `distributionManifestHash`, `policyRevisionHash`, `providerMinimumProfileRef`, `signingKeyRef` (child A's fixed `signing/unsigned-source-checkout`), `storeDriverRef`, `truthClass: "DAEMON_VERIFIED"` — and pass it to `reduceAndCommit`. `providerMinimumProfileRef` must be the ref the COMMITTED provider.probe registered, not a re-derived one, or core refuses on the mismatch. Remember core's `exact()` roster: an extra key refuses just as hard as a missing one, and the two hashes must match /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.

WIRE `project.activate` AS AN ASYNC ENTRY. In `daemon-command-async-entries.ts`, widen `AsyncCommandKind` with `"project.activate"`, add a receipts-measurement port to `AsyncCommandEntryOptions` (defaulting to child A's real `measureActivationReceipts` composed with `nodeGitRunner`, so an unconfigured daemon still measures rather than skipping), and return a third entry whose `asyncHandler` awaits the measurement and then calls `runBootstrapCommand(store, bytes, bootstrapTable, undefined, receipts)`, with the shared refusing sync `handler` the other two entries use. Follow the file's conditional-spread idiom for optional options. Keep it under 250 lines. Then update `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts`'s PAYLOAD_KEYS so `"project.activate"` no longer declares `["witness"]` — the payload carries no witness now — and update whatever roster test asserts that map, keeping it BIDIRECTIONAL (global rail 9): enumerate the served kinds from the dispatch seam, not only from the constant, so a deleted entry cannot shrink its own iteration and stay green.

TESTS — the refusal matrix and the accepted path. In `bootstrap-services.test.ts`, using `bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts` (teach its `send` helper to pass receipts; it calls `runBootstrapCommand` at :203 and :217): ARM 1 — a caller-supplied `witness` refuses ACTIVATION_WITNESS_CALLER_SUPPLIED @ DAEMON_INGRESS **and** the durable decision count is UNCHANGED (assert the count, not just the refusal — a rejected verdict that still reaches the store writes an audit row). ARM 2 (×6) — one arm per receipt member: exactly that member `known:false`, assert its exact code AND layer, the other five measured, and nothing committed. ARM 3 — all six measured: assert the COMMITTED event payload carries the actual measured values (repo toplevel + HEAD sha, provider CLI version, store path/driver, backup sha256), not merely that nine keys are present. ARM 4 — drive the REAL `reduceProject` with the minted witness and assert acceptance, proving core is satisfied without editing core. Verify every refusal arm goes red by mutating the production surface (swap one code for another); an arm that stays green is not testing its code (global rail 1).

MIGRATE THE TWO FAKERS. The daemon now refuses any caller-supplied witness, so both existing senders break unless they move in THIS commit. (1) `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/demo-seed-plan.ts:192` — change `build("project.activate", 2, { witness: activationWitness(input) })` to send NO witness. Keep the chain ORDER at :190-196 byte-identical (project.register -> project.bind_repository -> provider.probe -> project.activate -> policy.install ×3) — parent DoD 4 greps it. DELIBERATELY LEAVE `activationWitness` in demo-seed-payloads.ts EXPORTED AND UNTOUCHED: deleting it would drag demo-seed-payloads.ts AND `demo-seed-payloads.test.ts:124` (which asserts on it) into this row and breach its path cap. It becomes unused by the plan, which is correct and in scope; removing it is a follow-up, not this row. (2) `apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts:111-119` — `DEV_PAYLOADS["project.activate"]` drops its fake witness (artifact-1/backup-1/hex64("cafe")) to an empty payload. (3) `tests/e2e/control-room/board-chain.spec.ts` — update whatever it asserts about the project.activate dispatch report; that spec clicks the whole chain from an EMPTY store, so it is the test that actually proves the migration landed.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. Run and QUOTE THE COUNT LINES: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (must show demo-seed-*.test.ts green), `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (root lane — label it 'root lane only, apps/** not covered'; the root vitest include carries no apps/**, global rail 18). Grade every leg on its `Test Files N passed` line, never its exit code: `pnpm --filter <pkg>` prints 'No projects matched the filters' and EXITS 0 for a non-package (global rail 8). Prove the seed chain order is unchanged by grep, not by reading. Repo-wide legs are a path-attributed baseline (global rail 3): record merge-base failures, HEAD failures, and the delta intersected with this row's owned paths; disclose any foreign red verbatim. PORT CONTRACT — ActivationReceiptPorts (every member injected):
  backup: (storePath: string, destination: string) => Promise<ActivationBackupOutcome>
  committedProbeRef: () => Promise<string | null>
  env: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>
  fs: { exists(path): boolean; mkdir(path): void; readBytes(path): Uint8Array | null; stat(path): { readonly size: number } | null }

ActivationBackupOutcome = { ok: true; sha256: string; byteLength: number } | { ok: false; detail: string }.

nodeActivationReceiptPorts(overrides: Partial<ActivationReceiptPorts> = {}) supplies production implementations for ALL of them. Its committedProbeRef and installedPolicySliceRefs default to ABSENT (null / []) on purpose — an unwired caller gets an honest ACTIVATION_PROVIDER_UNMEASURED / ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED rather than an invented ref. CHILD B MUST OVERRIDE THOSE TWO or the handler can never mint a witness:
  committedProbeRef -> readProbe's envelopeRef (provider-profile/provider-profile-reader-checks.ts:113). The witness ref MUST equal the committed probe ref; reader-checks.ts:192-193 compares them.
  installedPolicySliceRefs -> installedSlices(stateOf(ledger, aggregateId)) (bootstrap-policy-services.ts:49); a slice's public address IS its content digest (:72-76).

ASSEMBLY: activationWitnessOf(receipts) -> { ok: true, witness } | { ok: false, refusals: readonly UnmeasuredReceipt[] }. It returns EVERY unmeasured member, never the first only, so the card can show all gaps at once. Each UnmeasuredReceipt carries { member, code, layer: "DAEMON_ACTIVATION_RECEIPTS", detail }. repositoryObservationOf(receipts) -> RepositoryObservation | null (null when repository is unmeasured); baseRevisionHash is sha256("git-sha1:<40hex>\n") because core's validHash demands 64 hex.

TWO THINGS THAT WILL BITE CHILD B:
1. activationWitnessOf ALSO refuses a measured member that arrives with an empty ref, a missing/empty hash (distribution, policy), or an empty detail (provider — that field IS the credentialRef). Added in child A's adversarial pass precisely because receipts reaching the handler from a parsed HTTP body are not necessarily the ones this daemon measured. The refusal names this layer and that member, not core's generic one.
2. truthClass is "DAEMON_VERIFIED". Core's strongTruth accepts ONLY DAEMON_VERIFIED | HUMAN_APPROVED (project-validation.ts:140) — there is no "VERIFIED" and no distinct "DEMO_VERIFIED" (demo-seed-payloads.ts:24 aliases it). Do not plan a truth-class refusal.

measureActivationReceipts never rejects: a throwing port becomes that member's refusal. It measures all six independently and never short-circuits.
